title: Installation of the Air Starter Motor and Dry Motoring Duct Leak Check
abstract: Installation of the air starter motor on the accessory gearbox pad and the duct leak check, run at the full extended dry motoring duration where the operator uses that cycle.

sections.purpose: This task installs the air starter motor on the accessory gearbox pad, connects the starter duct and does the dry motoring leak check that releases the starting system back to service.
sections.job_setup_note: Check the clamp standard before you start. The compensating clamp is required where the operator uses the extended dry motoring cycle, and an original clamp fitted on an aircraft that motors for ninety seconds will relax and leak within a few weeks. The leak check must be done at the duration the operator actually uses, not at the shorter default.
sections.procedure: 1. Make sure that the bleed system is depressurised and that the engine is cool. 2. Remove the gearbox pad blank and clean the pad face. 3. Inspect the starter splines and apply the spline grease specified in the instructions. CAUTION: DO NOT OVER-GREASE THE SPLINES. EXCESS GREASE IS THROWN INTO THE PAD SEAL AND WILL BE REPORTED AS AN OIL LEAK AFTER THE FIRST START. 4. Lift the starter on the sling and engage it squarely on the pad splines. 5. Install the attachment nuts hand tight and check that the starter flange sits flat. 6. Torque the nuts in the sequence given in the instructions, in two stages. 7. Where the heat shield tab is fitted, install it on the tube assembly D8010116441198 with the bolts EN290030-3C. 8. Remove the duct caps, position the duct and install the clamp PE187919-09. 9. Where the compensating clamp is fitted, set the band load with the calibrated tool to the value in the instructions. 10. Check the clearance between the tab and the heat shield at FIN 293ES. 11. Connect the electrical connector at the start valve nozzle FIN 2520ES and remove the label. WARNING: MAKE SURE THAT ALL PERSONNEL ARE CLEAR OF THE ENGINE INTAKE AND EXHAUST BEFORE THE DRY MOTORING RUN. 12. Do a dry motoring run for the full duration used by the operator. 13. Check the starter duct joint for leakage immediately after the run and again after the joint has cooled.
sections.close_out: Remove the drain tray and dispose of the fluid as scheduled waste. Close the fan cowl and check the latch engagement. Record the clamp standard, the band load and the leak check result on the maintenance record. Clear the technical log entry raised at removal.

type_data.effectivity_note: All aircraft. Steps 7 and 9 apply post MOD-155318 only.

safety_precautions: Make sure that all personnel are clear before the dry motoring run.
Confirm the clamp standard before installation.
